reviewer: web-host.lisp:131 has (fnn-store-error () :gone), and fnn-store-fault and fnn-store-indeterminate are subclasses of fnn-store-error (io.lisp:77, 92). An indeterminate outcome from fnn-owner-handle-chunk (the owner fences with exit 3 in owner.lisp:1791) is shown to the browser as session-gone, not as uncertain. The fnn-fault at web-host.lisp:128 ('owner consumed no octets') is raised outside any owner-serialized call, so this handler swallows it: the owner is never stopped and the fault becomes :gone while the node keeps serving. This breaks the rule that uncertain, refused and accepted stay distinct.
scenario: A browser POST is fed through fnn-owner-handle-chunk and the store's publication is ambiguous. fnn-store-indeterminate propagates (the owner fences with exit 3). The web face reports :gone and ACL2 renders the session-gone page, so the user is not told the outcome is uncertain and may repost. A host fault in the feed (line 128) is likewise rendered as a vanished session instead of a fault. This violates the rule that uncertain, refused and accepted stay distinct at every boundary.
title: fnn-web-feed turns fault, indeterminate and refusal into :gone
